title: How Brother Fox Was Too Smart
action_descriptions: The sly animal lies in the road to block the wagon.
The aggressive human shies the horse and hisses at the sly animal.
The aggressive human drives off, leaving the sly animal on the road.
The sly animal runs to the woods and lies again in the road.
The aggressive human drives, and the wheel nearly crushes the sly animal.
The sly animal leaps, lies again, and stretches out like a basket.
The aggressive human stops, examines the sly animal, and finds no injury.
The aggressive human decides to whip the sly animal.
The sly animal scrambles to its feet and escapes.

title: Mantharaka's
action_descriptions: The hunter captures the turtle, ties it to his bow, and sets off toward home.
The four friends devise a scheme to free the captured turtle.
The deer runs ahead of the hunter and pretends to be dead.
The crow pecks lightly at the deer's head to reinforce the feigned death.
The mouse hides beside the path and gnaws at the turtle's bonds.
The hunter sees the deer, sets down his burden, and approaches the scene.
As the hunter nears, the crow flies away and the deer jumps up, running into the forest.
The hunter curses, retraces his steps, and finds only the gnawed bonds.
The turtle disappears into a nearby swamp, free from capture.
All four friends reunite, having overcome the hunter's capture.

title: Reynard and Bruin
action_descriptions: The cunning fox and the trusting bear partner to share a home.
The cunning fox pretends to gossip and returns with honey.
The cunning fox tells the trusting bear names of children: Just-begun, Half-eaten, All-gone.
The trusting bear asks to join the feast, finds no honey, and accuses the fox.
The cunning fox claims the bear ate honey in sleep, and the fox smears honey on the bear's snout.
The cunning fox runs to a fish cart, pretends dead, the man takes him, the fox throws fish, and escapes.
The cunning fox shows the bear fishing, the bear fails, the man attacks the bear, and bear loses its tail.
The cunning fox gets a cream jug, the bear loses its tail, and the fox escapes.
The cunning fox and the trusting bear partnership ends, and the fox escapes.
The opportunistic man offers oxen to the bear, the fox offers geese, the hounds attack fox, and fox dies.

title: Brother Rabbit and the Gizzard-Eater
action_descriptions: The clever rabbit leaves home after a flood
The flood widens the creek, making it impassable
The clever rabbit calls for help from the ferry operator
The ferry operator is in a tree and cannot help directly
The clever rabbit calls the alligator, who wakes up
The alligator offers to carry the rabbit across the creek
The clever rabbit climbs onto the alligator's back
The alligator paddles across the creek, carrying the rabbit
The clever rabbit lands safely on the far bank

title: Dorani
action_descriptions: The daughter with golden hair cuts a lock of hair and throws it into the river.
The royal suitor finds the hair, demands marriage, and declares his intent.
The king arranges the marriage, and the daughter requests nightly return to her father's house.
The royal suitor marries, but the daughter remains silent and returns nightly to her father's house.
The royal suitor seeks help from a gardener and receives a magic powder for invisibility.
The royal suitor becomes invisible, follows the daughter to her father's house, and observes her rituals.
The royal suitor reports his observations to the daughter, but she remains silent.
The royal suitor continues to follow the daughter, who still speaks no words.
The royal suitor asks the daughter to prove love by not following her tonight.
The daughter speaks, the royal suitor hears, and they reconcile, ending the silence.

title: The Invisible Shepherd Boy
action_descriptions: The gray old man grants a bag that never fills and an invisible pelt to the pious shepherd son
The pious shepherd son leaves his pasture and travels to the capital city
The king has twelve daughters, eleven of whom wear many shoes nightly, causing cost and rumors
The king offers his youngest daughter to whoever solves the mystery of the shoe-wearing
Many suitors arrive, are ridiculed by the daughters, and withdraw in shame
The pious shepherd son, wearing the invisible pelt, slips into the daughters' bedroom at night
The mysterious spirit enters, wakes the daughters, and they prepare by putting shoes into a bag
The pious shepherd son awakens the youngest daughter, who then agrees to join them
The mysterious spirit places a basin; the daughters rub its contents, wings grow, and they all fly
They fly to a copper forest, drink, and the shepherd son collects a cup and leaves a copper twig in his bag
They fly to a silver forest, drink, and the shepherd son collects a silver cup and leaves a silver twig in his bag
They fly to a golden forest, drink, and the shepherd son collects a golden cup and leaves a golden twig in his bag
They reach a mountain cliff; the mysterious spirit opens a passage, and they enter a hall of fairy-like splendor
In the hall, fairy-youths appear, music plays, and the group enjoys a ball before returning home
The king learns of the events, summons the daughters, and evidence proves their guilt
The king fulfills his promise; the youngest daughter marries the shepherd son, and the eleven daughters are burned

title: Blue-Beard
action_descriptions: The husband carries a basket on his back.
The husband goes to houses begging for food.
When pretty girls give him food, the husband grabs them in the basket and runs away.
The husband brings the captured women to his large place.
The husband gives the captured women keys, tells them everything belongs to them except one room, warns not to enter.
The husband marries seven times, all wives are sisters.
While the husband is away, the seventh wife takes the keys and enters the forbidden room.
The seventh wife finds all her sisters dead in a pile.
The seventh wife is excited, drops the keys, and gets them bloody.
The husband returns and demands the keys.
The seventh wife hides the keys for several days and refuses to give them.
The seventh wife eventually gives the keys to the husband.
The husband tells the seventh wife to say a prayer.
The seventh wife prays seven times.
The seventh wife's seven brothers arrive just as the husband goes to kill her.
The husband runs away into the woods and is never seen again.

title: Loppi and Lappi
action_descriptions: The husband and wife quarrel over trivial matters.
The higher being appears and offers three wishes.
The couple decide to use the wishes wisely.
They spend days thinking and become harmonious.
The husband and wife wish for a sausage to accompany soup.
A sausage falls onto the wife's nose and becomes flesh.
The husband angrily wishes for the Evil One to harm the wife.
The sausage becomes a fleshy growth on the wife's nose.
The wife wishes for the sausage to disappear.
All three wishes are used and the couple returns to poverty.
The couple expects the higher being to return but she does not.
The moral that failing to seize luck loses it forever is implied.

title: The Woodman's Three Wishes
action_descriptions: The woodman chops a huge oak when a fairy appears.
The woodman consents to spare the tree, and the fairy promises three wishes.
The woodman forgets the fairy by evening.
The woodman wishes for a link of hog's pudding at night.
A rustling in the chimney brings the pudding to the woodman's feet.
The woodman tells his wife about the pudding.
The wife, incensed, wishes the pudding to attach to her nose.
The pudding sticks tightly to the wife's nose, impossible to remove.
The woodman wishes the pudding off, fulfilling his third wish.
The fairy's promise of wishes ends, leaving the woodman without further wishes.

title: Vedabbha-Jataka: Misguided Effort
action_descriptions: The self-willed Brother ignores counsel and is cut in two.
The brahmin learns of a charm that summons treasure when planets align.
The brahmin and the pupil travel to a forest where robbers capture them.
The brahmin repeats the charm, causing treasure to rain, and robbers take it.
A second band of robbers captures the brahmin again, cuts him, and kills the first band.
The robbers fight among themselves, reducing their numbers to two survivors.
The two survivors plot to kill each other, both die.
The pupil returns, finds corpses, and realizes the cause of the destruction.
The pupil burns the Brother's body, offers flowers, and reflects on the moral.
The pupil concludes that misguided self-will leads to ruin for all.

title: The Emperor's Daughter and the Swineherd
action_descriptions: The royal daughter announces that a man who can guess her birthmarks will be her husband.
The swineherd offers a piglet after the royal daughter reveals a birthmark on the royal daughter's forehead.
The swineherd offers a second piglet after the royal daughter reveals a birthmark on the royal daughter's breast.
The swineherd offers a third piglet after the royal daughter reveals a birthmark on the royal daughter's knee.
The Turk arrives and claims to know the royal daughter's birthmarks.
The royal daughter allows both suitors to guess the royal daughter's birthmarks; both correctly identify them.
The royal daughter decides to let both suitors stay overnight to determine the winner.
The swineherd uses trickery to make the Turk believe the Turk is eating dung, causing the Turk to act foolishly.
The royal daughter chooses the swineherd as husband after the Turk's foolishness.
The swineherd becomes the royal daughter's son-in-law and lives happily with the royal family.

title: The Nobleman's Daughter and the Shepherd
action_descriptions: The noble daughter shows her birthmark to the shepherd.
The shepherd volunteers to herd 300 hares.
The 300 hares escape from the shepherd.
The little gray helper gives the shepherd a flute.
The shepherd recovers all hares with the flute.
The noble daughter, mother, and father disguise themselves and beg a hare.
The shepherd recovers the hares with the flute, thwarting the disguised suitors.
The group of suitors fails to reveal an unknown truth.
The shepherd tells the price of the hares, embarrassing the noble family.
The noble daughter and parents declare the shepherd the winner, and he marries her.

title: The Pig-Boy and the Princess
action_descriptions: The pig-boy teaches piglets to dance with a flute.
The pig-boy negotiates with the princess for a piglet.
The princess receives a piglet but it does not dance.
The pig-boy gives the princess a flute, enabling piglets to dance.
The pig-boy leaves with no piglets or flute.
The king announces a deadly riddle to find a bride.
The pig-boy meets a priest, and they travel together.
The priest answers first, and the king spares his life.
The pig-boy answers correctly, winning the princess.
The priest leaves ashamed after failing to win the princess.
The pig-boy marries the princess, ending the quest.

title: Jack o' Kent and the Devil: The Tops and the Butts
action_descriptions: The clever laborer and the cunning bargain partner agree to split wheat and straw.
The clever laborer harvests wheat, the cunning bargain partner receives straw.
The clever laborer and the cunning bargain partner agree to split turnips and tops.
The clever laborer harvests turnips, the cunning bargain partner receives tops.
The clever laborer and the cunning bargain partner agree to split grass and hay.
The clever laborer places harrow tines in grass to damage the cunning bargain partner's scythe.
The cunning bargain partner's scythe catches in tines, distracting the partner.
The clever laborer mows grass, securing most hay while the partner is distracted.
The clever laborer and the cunning bargain partner agree to split threshing: the laborer gets bottoms, the partner tops.
The clever laborer sets a hurdle for the partner to thresh on.
The cunning bargain partner threshes on the hurdle, while the clever laborer collects grain on the floor.

title: The Farmer and the Devil on Island of the Popefigs
action_descriptions: The devil proposes an unfair profit sharing contract.
The laborer accepts the contract.
They harvest wheat: the laborer above ground, the devil below ground.
The laborer sells above ground produce, earning money.
The devil sells below ground produce, fails, and is jeered.
The devil accuses the laborer of cheating.
The laborer explains the devil's plan to cheat, revealing above ground produce is rotten.
The devil acknowledges being cheated and ends the business.
The devil proposes a new contract for turnips: devil gets below ground, laborer above ground.
They harvest turnips: the laborer above ground, the devil below ground.
The laborer sells turnips, earning money.
The devil sells nothing, is jeered.
The devil accuses the laborer again.
The laborer explains the devil's cheating again.
The devil concedes and ends the business.

title: The Story of Tam M'Kechan
action_descriptions: The poor jockey decides to test the legend by spending a night at the mill.
The poor jockey sets a fire, lights pipes, and goes alone into the mill.
The poor jockey disappears, leaving ashes, an overturned stool, and no trace.
The young farmer and the supportive miller arrive, find the mill empty, and notice no sign of the jockey.
The young farmer spends the night, hears music, and sees fairies dancing near the fire.
The fairy creature enters, speaks, and offers a name to the young farmer.
The young farmer, enraged, strikes the fairy creature, causing it to burn and die.
The fairies swarm, destroy the mill, and leave the young farmer alone in the dark.

title: Kilgrim Bridge
action_descriptions: The supernatural builder promises a bridge that will defy floods.
The supernatural builder demands that the first living creature crossing be sacrificed to the judge.
The inhabitants debate who should be the victim.
The wise shepherd swims the river and whistles for the loyal dog.
The loyal dog, unaware, crosses the bridge and becomes the first living creature to cross.
The supernatural judge claims the loyal dog as sacrifice.
The bridge remains intact, but the loyal dog is sacrificed.
The inhabitants name the spot Kill Grim Bridge.

title: An Unusual Ride
action_descriptions: The father rides the donkey while the son walks.
A traveler advises the father to let the son ride.
The father climbs off the donkey and lets the son ride.
A traveler advises the son to let the father walk.
The father and son both mount the donkey and ride together.
A traveler advises to remove both from the donkey.
The father and son climb off, and all three walk with the donkey in the middle.
A traveler advises to tie the donkey's legs and carry it.
The father ties the donkey's front legs, the son ties its back legs, and they carry it on their shoulders.
They reach home carrying the donkey on their shoulders.

title: The Blind Men and the Elephant
action_descriptions: Heretical disputing monks enter the city and quarrel over doctrines.
Heretical disputing monks wound each other with sharp words.
Heretical disputing monks approach the teacher and report the quarrels.
The teacher comments on the ignorance of the disputing monks.
The king orders the blind observers to be gathered.
The king brings an elephant before the blind observers.
Blind observers feel various parts of the elephant.
Blind observers describe the elephant based on their sensations.
Blind observers quarrel over their differing descriptions of the elephant.
The king is delighted by the observers' quarrel.
The teacher parallels the blind observers' quarrel with the disputing monks.

title: The Purchase of the Horse's Egg
action_descriptions: The leader and disciples decide to buy a horse.
The leader and disciples realize the price is too high.
The leader and disciples lose their cow and search for it.
The seeker finds horse eggs near a lake.
The group decides to buy the eggs at low price.
The skeptical companion doubts hatching the egg; the leader proposes sitting on it.
They negotiate with farmer and buy an egg.
They set out with the egg; the seeker carries it.
The egg breaks, hare escapes, they chase but fail.
They return exhausted; the leader declares the horse lost.

title: Little Louse and Little Flea
action_descriptions: The louse falls into eggshell and burns to death.
The flea cries loudly.
The door speaks to the flea.
The broom speaks to the door.
The broom sweeps furiously.
The cart speaks to the broom.
The cart runs furiously.
The manure pile burns in flames.
The tree speaks to the manure pile.
The tree shakes itself.
The girl observes and speaks to the tree.
The girl breaks her water pitcher.
The spring speaks to the girl.
The spring flows furiously.
All drown in water.

title: Dathera Dad (Addy)
action_descriptions: The farmer's wife prepares pudding and places it on the fire to boil.
The pudding jumps as the water begins to boil.
The pudding rolls across the floor.
A traveling tinker arrives at the door.
The farmer's wife gives the rolling pudding to the tinker.
The tinker places the pudding into his budget and slings it over his back.
The tinker trudges along the road while the pudding keeps rolling in the budget.
The pudding breaks into pieces.
A fairy child emerges from the broken pudding and cries for its father.
